scope: Symbolic equations only; no model/array/fixture run; normalization identities assume nonzero vectors outside numerical epsilon-clamp region.

same_student_peers.condition: Every normalized same-class student embedding equalsu_c. Q rows supported on other same-class TRAIN nodes; full common denominator excludes exactself.
same_student_peers.claim: For every sameclass positive pair, both query and peer tangent derivatives of cosine are0. Thus the weighted-positive gradient is0 regardless of Q row ratios, including incoming peer-key contributions; denominator/otherclass/ownCE gradients can remain. Q-specific cotangents exist in score space but its Jacobian kills them.
same_student_peers.limit: No observed collapse or full training stationarity inferred. Away from coincidence, Q can matter; higher-order curvature can also differ.

fixed_keys.notation: A:R^128→R^300 shared trainable bias-free map; z_i=Ah_i; q_i=z_i/||z_i||. Fixed normalized keys k_j (zero key for zero signature), E_i=all other TRAIN, Q_i rowmass1 supportedon sameclass E_i.
fixed_keys.loss: L_i=log Σ_(j∈E_i) exp(q_i·k_j/τ) − q_i·μ_Qi/τ; μ_Qi=Σ_jQ_ijk_j. Define p_ij=softmax_(E_i)(q_i·k_j/τ), μ_pi=Σ_jp_ijk_j.
fixed_keys.A_gradient: ∂L_i/∂A=(∂L_i/∂z_i)h_iᵀ; batch/route mean sums these terms with exact declared loss weights.
fixed_keys.target_difference_at_same_q_keys_support: For fixed q,K,E, gradient_h(Qa)−gradient_h(Qb)=−Aᵀ(I−qqᵀ)(μ_Qa−μ_Qb)/(τ||Ah||). Nonzero iff the projected target-mean difference survives.
fixed_keys.different_route_banks: For K_m differing by graph context, both μ_p and μ_Q change; complete gradients can cancel. Only the isolated target contribution has the simple mean-difference form.
fixed_keys.symbolic_witness: q=e1, A=I, fixed sameclass keys e1/e2, Qa=(3/4,1/4),Qb=(1/4,3/4). Projected targetmean difference is−e2/2, so the two query gradients differ by e2/(2τ||z||), although normalized students may all coincide. This is an analytic witness, not an executed toy or actual-data result.

necessary_limits: Distinct Q rows may have the same μ_Q when their difference lies in the key-matrix nullspace
A targetmean difference paralleltoq is removed by the normalization tangent
Aᵀ may annihilate a remaining tangent, and native parameter Jacobians can further annihilate/cancel it
Fixed feature keys can themselves be equal withinclass, making weighted means identical
A shared auxiliary projection can absorb alignment changes in directions unused by the classifier
Complete denominator terms can cancel target gradients, and mixedCE optimization has its own tradeoff
Normalizedqueries withz=0 or inside epsilon clamp require a different derivative; no use of singular1/||z|| claim
fixed_projection_degenerate_case: Two identical h queries with opposite tangent mean-errorsv and−v, Aᵀv=0: individual h gradients vanish and their shared A outer-product gradients cancel. Therefore fixed keys do not guarantee avoidance/escape of class coincidence even when targetmeans differ.
Q_information_reduction: For fixed linear-dot-product keys, the entire Q dependence of L is exactly μ_Q. Different rows with the same keymean have identical loss for every query. This does not transfer the full weighted target distribution or its pairwise geometry.
matched_positive_alignment: R_i=Σ_jQ_ij(1−q_i·k_j)/τ=(1−q_i·μ_Qi)/τ. Same target/query gradients as the weighted-positive part; L_i=R_i+logΣ_Eexp(q_i·k_j/τ)−1/τ. Do not normalize μ_Q or use an unweighted cosine-to-normalized-mean control, which changes perrow amplitude.
finite_target_fit: CrossclassQ zeros cannot equal finite strictly-positive full softmax. Queryrank/norm and fixedkey geometry further constrain fitting. Asymmetry removes the symmetricpeer score-Jacobian obstruction only under the stated conditions, not every realizability/optimization obstruction.
